ErrorKind.description:
Why a call failed: the error reply's `errorKind`. `too_large`: the
payload exceeds 4096 bytes. `unknown_method`: no such method.
`forbidden`: only the TV app may change Prysm. `removing`: the service is
being removed. `invalid_request`: the payload is not the method's request.
`wrong_package`: the other package's method (`setTarget` on slim,
`setEnabled` on full). `invalid_preferences`: a preference the installed
package does not have. `save_failed`: the preferences could not be saved.
`internal`: the service could not read the call or send its reply. Open:
an app reads a kind it does not know as a refusal and shows `errorText`.

ErrorReply.description:
Any failed call. LS2's own replies (for example for a method that is not
registered) carry no `errorKind`; an app reads that as an unknown kind.

FailureKind.description:
What a failure is, so the app can offer the matching fix. `encoder`
(slim): the encoder the receiver requested could not start or failed;
the receiver is told, and another encoding chosen in its portal may work.
`receiver` (slim): the receiver is unavailable (not lighting, unreachable,
or its name does not resolve); the worker keeps reconnecting. `version`
(slim): Prysm speaks another capture stream version; the older one needs
updating, and the worker keeps reconnecting. `replaced` (slim): another
TV took over the stream at Prysm; this one stopped sending until the
worker restarts (capture stopped and started, the TV waking, or a new
Prysm address). `receiver_failed` (slim): Prysm's receiving source failed
with this TV's stream (a refusal, a keyframe that does not decode, no
decoder), and Prysm shows why; the worker released the capture and keeps
reconnecting. `preferences`: the TV's saved preferences could not be
read; the service runs with the defaults and keeps the file until the app
saves preferences. `other`: anything else. Open: an app reads a kind it
does not know as `other`.

FullWorker.description: The full package's worker process, as `{ "phase": … }`.

capturing.description: Lighting runs and frames arrive (false while it waits for video).

fps.description:
Frames per second over about the last second, rounded, while
lighting runs; 0 while it waits for frames.

portal.description: The portal's LAN address once the worker reported it.

oneOf.description: Being stopped; the portal may still answer until it exits.

portal.description: The portal's LAN address the worker last reported.

oneOf.description: Waiting before the next start after a failure.

seconds.description:
Whole seconds until the next start, rounded up, when this state
was sent (at least 1). The app counts down from when it received
it; no clock is shared.

subscribe.description: Keep sending the state on every change.

LightingTarget.description: What the user wants the LEDs to do.

Package.description:
The installed package (both install as the same app), what the user asked
of it and its worker process, as `{ "flavor": … }`.

oneOf.description: `prysm-webos`: capture, processing, WLED and the portal on the TV.

target.description: The engine's target, including changes made in the portal.

oneOf.description: `prysm-webos-slim`: capture forwarded to a headless Prysm.

enabled.description: Frames should flow to the receiver.

Preferences.description:
The installed package's preferences: the `setPreferences` request
(complete, every field optional, an unset one absent) and the published
`preferences`. Fields marked "Slim only" must stay unset in the full
package. The file is [`PreferencesFile`].

autostart.description:
Start when the service starts: the full package starts screen sync,
the slim package streams to its receiver.

prysm_address.description:
Slim only: the headless Prysm's address, such as
`http://192.168.1.20:8787` or `https://prysm.example.com` (through a
reverse proxy). The TV streams its picture there, and the TV app
links to its portal. Only the syntax is checked when saved; the TV
resolves a host name at every connection attempt, and one that does
not resolve is reported as the receiver wait.

enabled.description: Frames should flow to the receiver.

target.description: What the lights do: off, screen sync, or their own effects.

SlimLink.description:
Where the slim worker's stream to the receiver stands, as `{ "state": … }`.
`starting`: no connection attempt yet. `sending`: connected, frames go
out in `encoding` (the one the receiver requested, set in the desktop
portal), `fps` per second (0 while none come). `paused`: the
receiver stopped the stream because its lighting is off; the TV capture
is released until a receiver takes a connection again, not a failure.
`waiting`: the receiver is unavailable (`failure.kind` `receiver`).
`failed`: the encoder, version, replaced or receiver-failed failure. The
state's own `failure` is the one to show.

fps.description: Frames sent per second over about the last second, rounded.

SlimWorker.description: The slim package's worker process, as `{ "phase": … }`.

capturing.description:
Frames were sent in the last second (so also just after the
stream ended).

link.description:
Where the uplink to the receiver stands, as the worker last
reported it.

oneOf.description: Waiting before the next start after a failure.

seconds.description:
Whole seconds until the next start, rounded up, when this state
was sent (at least 1). The app counts down from when it received
it; no clock is shared.

failure.description:
The current failure (or, slim, the receiver wait): what it is and
its message with the causes.

log.description: The latest worker stderr lines, oldest first (at most 20).

State.description:
The `getState` reply and subscription payload (plus LS2's `returnValue`):
the fields both packages have, and the installed package's own
([`Package`], tagged by `flavor`).

subscribed.description: On `getState` and subscription updates: whether the caller is subscribed.

StateReply.description: A successful state reply: [`State`] with LS2's `returnValue`.

StreamEncoding.description:
How the sender encodes the frames it sends: `h264_hardware`, the
sender's hardware H.264 encoder (the webOS TV's), about 2 Mbit/s;
`h264_software`, OpenH264 on the sender's CPU, about 2 Mbit/s; `raw`,
uncompressed NV12 pixels, about 21 Mbit/s at 320x180 and 30 fps. Exactly
this encoder is used: one that cannot start or fails stops the stream,
and the sender never switches to another.

WorkerFailure.description: A failure: what it is and its message with the causes.

message.description: What failed, with its cause chain (cut to 1 KiB).
